trust_decision.summary: Cranelift's wasm translator decides where compiled guest code may yield to the host (epoch callback / out-of-fuel) during a bulk operation; at the pinned commit it yields mid-operation, after bounds checks and raw-address derivation, so a host callback that grows memory/tables or runs GC invalidates pointers the rest of the operation still uses; the fix moves the single preemption point before bounds checks (or before allocation for uninitialized entities).

landing_point.why: raw_bulk_memory_operation is documented as the place that chunks bulk copies with preemption checks between chunks (func_environ.rs:3564-3568); 'preemption during bulk operations' leads straight to it.

fix_sites.entry_point: wasm opcodes memory.copy / memory.fill / memory.init (and byte-array fill/copy memset path) compiled via Module::new
fix_sites.module_kind: compiler codegen helper (chunked libcall loop removed)

fix_sites.entry_point: wasm table.fill / array.fill / array.new per-element fill loop
wasm memory.copy, memory.init, table.copy, table.init, array.copy, array.init_data, array.init_elem (translate_entity_copy)
wasm table.copy / array.copy per-element forward loop
wasm table.copy / array.copy per-element backward loop
wasm table.grow (grow libcall then fill of new slots)
Instance::new / Linker::instantiate running compiled module-initialization code (table with non-null init expr)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: crates/cranelift/src/func_environ.rs:2647 (table.grow composes a grow libcall with translate_table_fill marked initialized:true); also crates/cranelift/src/func_environ/gc.rs:776-790 (array.new allocates then fills) and crates/cranelift/src/func_environ.rs:5971-5980 (instantiation-time table init fill)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: table.grow, array.new and instantiation-time table initialization are 'grow/allocate/instantiate' operations, not the bulk copy/fill opcodes the report names, and they reach the yield only indirectly through a shared fill helper, so a solver who moves the check to the top of translate_entity_fill/copy considers them covered — yet for uninitialized entities the check must sit before the grow/alloc call, not inside the fill.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Long bulk operations must still be charged fuel proportional to length and still observe epoch deadlines (time-slicing / OutOfFuel trap before the op); small constant-length ops (<=128) skip the explicit check and the inline memcpy fast path must keep working. Deleting the checks entirely, or checking after the op, breaks fuel accounting and the existing disas/fuel tests.

O6_input_shapes: memory vs table vs GC array entity
initialized destination (fill/copy) vs uninitialized destination (table.grow new slots, array.new*, instantiation table init)
constant length (folded into static fuel, check skipped when <=128) vs dynamic length
i32 vs i64 (memory64/table64) length; i64 cost clamped to i64::MAX so a huge/negative table64 delta cannot mint fuel
memset-able fill value vs per-element loop

O8b_injection_room.sibling: active element-segment init loop (translate_table_set per element) gaining a per-element translate_loop_header after the up-front bounds check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: upstream later added variable fuel cost to exactly this loop (latest/crates/cranelift/src/func_environ.rs:6268), so a per-element check placed after the bounds check is a natural mistake.
